section.t: B'S"D

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The verse "Great will be the glory of this latter house more than the first" has two interpretations: simply referring to the Second Temple, and in the Zohar referring to the future Third Temple which will be eternal.
section.t: "Great will be the glory of this latter house more than the first,"
and there are two explanations of this.
The simple explanation is
that "this latter house" refers to the Second Temple, which was greater than the First Temple in construction and in years.
And in the Zohar
it is stated that "this latter house" refers to the Third Temple, which will be built speedily in our days, and it will be greater than the First Temple and the Second Temple.
For both of them are included in
("than the")
first,
because neither of them had permanence,
but the Third Temple will endure with eternal permanence.
And this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said:
"Not like Avraham, of whom it is written 'mountain,' nor like Yitzchak, of whom it is written 'field,' but like Yaakov, who called it 'house.'"
For the First Temple corresponds to Avraham, the Second Temple corresponds to Yitzchak, and the Third Temple corresponds to Yaakov.
And it is explained in Likkutei Torah
that the connection of the Third Temple to Yaakov is because the attribute of Yaakov is truth,
and truth is that which is not subject to interruption
or change.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Although the Sages spoke of the Temple, Likkutei Torah applies the same three-part pattern to the three redemptions, with the third redemption being eternal, linked to the Third Temple's superiority.
section.t: B)
Now, although in the aforementioned statement of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,
("not like Avraham, etc.")
the discussion is about the Holy Temple,
the language in Likkutei Torah there is: "There are three redemptions—
the first redemption in the merit of Avraham, the second redemption in the merit of Yitzchak, the third redemption in the merit of Yaakov."
And it explains there that the third redemption is an eternal redemption.
And the simple explanation of this is,
that one of the fundamentals of redemption is the building of the Holy Temple.
And by virtue of the added elevation in the Holy Temple,
the redemption is more exalted.
Therefore, in Likkutei Torah, the superiority of the third redemption is linked with the superiority of the Third Temple.
